outcome: venous blood levels of red blood cells, hemoglobin, and hematocrit
incidence of hypothermia, hypoglycemia, respiratory distress, septicemia, feeding intolerance, polycythemia, and hyperbilirubinemia requiring phototherapy during hospitalization

cohort: 163 preterm infants with a gestational age of 34-36 weeks + 6
finding: Delayed cord clamping increased hemoglobin levels at birth and at 5-6 months after birth and improved the oxygen circulation supply to the organs of preterm infants.
mod_finding: Delayed cord clamping improved the prognosis of preterm infants.
